newsitem.title: UK: UK "wise man" Congdon calls for 100 bp rate rise.
newsitem.headline: UK "wise man" Congdon calls for 100 bp rate rise.

text.p: Tim Congdon, a member of the UK Treasury's panel of independent economic advisers, called for an increase of a full percentage point in official interest rates from the present 5.75 percent, the Evening Standard newspaper reported.
"I am now in favour of increasing interest rates," the newspaper quoted him as saying. "If rates are raised soon, that will avert the need for more drastic moves at a later date."
Congdon added that a rise "of about one percent would be the right thing to do."
The Bank of England has been calling since July for a rise in interest rates to 6.0 percent to head off what it sees as the threat of resurgent inflation in the next two years.
But Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, who has cut rates four times since December, has so far rejected the Bank's advice.
The next monthly monetary meeting will be on October 30.
Congdon has often been at odds with other members of the advisory panel, notably Patrick Minford, who argues that inflation is under control.
